newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Missing 17-year-old girl turns up in Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Missing 17-year-old girl turns up in Belgium.

text.p: A 17-year-old girl whose disappearance sparked off a full-scale police hunt in Belgium walked into a central Brussels police station on Monday, Belga news agency said.
Belgium is still traumatised by a paedophile scandal and the discovery over the past year of the bodies of five young girls, kidnapped and murdered.
Lamya Zouboudi disappeared while out shopping on June 28. Belgian police launched a search only last Thursday and were criticised by her family for being slow to start the hunt.
Her adoptive parents had insisted she was not a runaway. But Belga said Zouboudi told police on Monday she had indeed run away from home because of family problems.
The slow police response prompted comparisons in the Belgian media with the failings of the hunt for eight-year-old Loubna Benaissa.
Loubna, who went missing in 1992, was found dead in March this year, stuffed into a steel trunk in the basement of a Brussels garage.
Police had taken days to start investigations despite the family's pleas, and had even searched the garage where her body was eventually found.
Loubna's body was the fifth such find in seven months in a paedophile scandal that is still rocking Belgium and has triggered wide-ranging reform of the police and justice system.
Police are still searching for at least seven other children who have disappeared without trace over the years.
